title: EID Parry India Ltd - 500125 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 refinery loss widened to Rs 293 crore (vs Rs 99 crore), while PSRIPL refinery closure drove Rs 600 crore of parent equity infusion into loan repayment.
summary.overview: Sugar performed better YoY: crushing rose to 17.75 LMT (17.62 LMT), recovery improved to 11.19% (10.89%), and sugar revenue rose about 14% to Rs 466 crore on higher exports and release quota. Refinery (PSRIPL) revenue was flat at Rs 1,006 crore but the loss widened to Rs 293 crore, and the unit is being closed, with bank loans of $49 million and $29 million repaid in April and May and the final $1.4 million due in June 2026. The CPG business shrank 48% to Rs 115 crore as management deliberately recalibrated channels and margins. Management gave no timeline for dividend resumption.

segments.name: Sugar
segments.commentary: Crushed 17.75 LMT in Q4 over about 77 days, producing 1.74 LMT sugar (1.55 LMT YoY). Sales were 97,000 MT including about 6,000 MT exports (73,000 MT YoY); closing stock 1.92 LMT valued at about Rs 39/kg.

segments.name: Co-generation
segments.commentary: Generated 1,499 LU (1,450 LU YoY) and exported 845 LU (732 LU YoY) at Rs 4.57/unit, generating Rs 66 crore revenue.

segments.name: Distillery / ethanol
segments.commentary: Produced 452 LL (438 LL YoY) and sold 404 LL: 150 LL ENA and 64 LL ethanol, plus other volumes, for Rs 275 crore revenue at Rs 64.25/litre average realisation.

segments.name: Refinery (PSRIPL)
segments.commentary: Production 1.69 LMT (1.17 LMT YoY) and sales 2.3 LMT (2.05 LMT). Revenue Rs 1,006 crore, loss Rs 293 crore. Operations closed as of 31 March 2026; SEZ exit expected by 30 September 2026.

segments.name: Consumer products (CPG)
segments.commentary: Turnover Rs 115 crore, down 48% from Rs 195 crore, due to deliberate channel optimisation and a shift away from low-margin rice and pulses toward sweeteners.

segments.name: Nutra (Nutra India and Valensa)
segments.commentary: Turnover Rs 13 crore vs Rs 9 crore, aided by US exports after the US tariff settled at 10%. Valensa has two product launches planned (prostate and dermal health).

guidance_outlook: PSRIPL loan repayments: $49 million (Rs 460 crore) paid by 24 April and $29 million (Rs 272 crore) by 15 May 2026; the final $1.4 million is due in June 2026, funded from PSRIPL receivables, which completes all PSRIPL loan obligations by 30 June 2026.
Parent EID Parry has infused about Rs 600 crore into PSRIPL's payment obligations to date.
SEZ exit formalities are expected to be completed by 30 September 2026; the plant and machinery liquidation process has started with vendors and possibly tenders.
Only capex this year is a new jaggery facility of about Rs 45 crore; no other capex planned, with focus on cost and efficiency.
CPG aims to break even within 6-8 quarters and reach a good single-digit EBITDA margin by the end of the decade; value-added sweetener products are targeted at 30%+ gross margin.
Management expects ethanol blending to rise (E30 signalled); the company could move from about 16 crore litres toward 17 crore litres if blending improves. Sugar MSP increase considered unlikely.
Sugar exports banned until 30 September 2026 per management.
capex_capacity: New jaggery facility, about Rs 45 crore, the only capex planned this year.
Crushing ran about 77 days in Q4 (76 days YoY); recovery 11.19% vs 10.89%.
Distillery produced 452 LL in Q4 (438 LL YoY), with capacity utilisation expected to rise toward 17 crore litres annually if blending increases.
Tamil Nadu sugarcane planting is expected to rise 10-15%, though TN is constrained by competition from paddy and other crops.
Refinery operations closed; plant and machinery liquidation under way.
demand_pricing: Global white sugar fell from about USD 500/t in 2025 to about USD 420/t by early 2026; raw sugar fell from about USD 0.80/lb to about USD 0.14/lb.
India SY2025-26: gross production 31 MMT, 3 MMT diverted to ethanol, 28 MMT domestic consumption, 0.7 MMT exports, closing stock 4.25 MMT.
Q4 sugar realisation was flat at Rs 39.28/kg YoY despite higher volumes.
Power tariff rose to Rs 4.57/unit from Rs 4.38, and distillery realisation fell to Rs 64.25/litre from Rs 66.98.

Management says the Appellate Tribunal tariff order (Sept 2025) does not apply to EID Parry because power is mainly sold on IEX; some past-period benefit may be possible, but no income was recognised and it is not seen as substantial.

qa_highlights.question: What are the CPG plans, value-added products and margin profile versus rice and pulses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is exiting low-margin staples (rice, pulses) to a few channels and focusing on jaggery, brown sugar variants and premium whites. Value-added products are expected to reach 30%+ gross margin. New sweet product launches are planned later in the year.

qa_highlights.question: Any acquisition progress in food/FMCG?
qa_highlights.answer: Management named ethnic snacking and culinary convenience as target segments. It is in talks on entry routes but gave no deal details; strengthening the current model comes first.

qa_highlights.question: Nutra division scale-up and margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: No new Nutra India launches. Valensa is the growth lever, with two launches (prostate and dermal health), a reoriented strategy and a new management team. Expected to lift both top line and bottom line.

qa_highlights.question: Any positive ethanol policy change post the West Asia crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: The government has signalled E30 through BIS; positive action is expected via allocations in the new ethanol year. Pricing action is unlikely, but blending increases are expected.

qa_highlights.question: How is capital allocated after the refinery restructuring?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus is on CPG (brand building, distribution and A&P, with no real capex) and on cost and efficiency in the core business. Only capex is the Rs 45 crore jaggery facility.

qa_highlights.question: When will CPG break even and what share of profit could it reach?
qa_highlights.answer: Break-even in 6-8 quarters and a good single-digit EBITDA margin by the end of the decade. No share-of-profit target was given.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not give a timeline and said it is focused on strengthening the business operations.

risks_watch: Refinery (PSRIPL) losses, SEZ exit completion by 30 September 2026, and the plant liquidation proceeds.
Continued loss-making Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh sugar operations, with cane supply dwindling in AP.
CPG revenue decline (-48%) and whether the recalibrated margin model reaches break-even in 6-8 quarters.
Ethanol blending and allocation decisions for the new ethanol year, and sugar export ban through 30 September 2026.
No dividend timeline given; shareholder concern was raised on the call.
Possible tax benefit from the Tribunal tariff order not yet accounted for, with past periods still under assessment.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on sugar operations and ethanol policy outlook but cautious and vague on profitability and dividends. It deflected the takeover and dividend questions with no timelines, and said it would focus on the core business.
key_quotes: The intent is to break even within the next 6-8 quarters and exit this decade with a good single-digit percentage EBITDA on this business.
Our Karnataka operations remain a very, very critical and core area of focus. They are very positive EBITDA generating.
The only CAPEX that we are doing this year is largely the new Jaggery facility. That is about a 45-odd crore CAPEX which we are doing.

growth.why: No revenue growth guided; management says it will "hunker down" on cost and efficiency with only a Rs 45 crore jaggery facility as capex, refinery (PSRIPL) closed, CPG breakeven targeted in 6-8 quarters, and ethanol capacity could move from 16 to 17 crore litres only if blending improves.
